summary: FRONTEND RE-TEST of Credit Cards stacked carousel tap-target fix (iteration 12). PARTIAL PASS. Measurement passes: with 3 collapsed cards (COLLAPSED_PEEK=96, PEEK_VISIBLE=48, marginBottom=-48), each collapsed card presents exactly a 48px unobstructed visible strip (verified via getBoundingClientRect: tops at y=100, 148, 196). TAP-ROUTING BUG STILL PRESENT: tapping the MIDDLE card's visible strip does NOT expand that card. Using document.elementFromPoint over the full strip range, pixels y=110..190 ALL resolve to the first card (card-77062a43/Charlie) because Charlie has zIndex=3 and its full 96px hit box (y=100-196) blocks Bravo's 48px visible strip (y=148-196). Similarly, taps on Alpha's visible top half (y=196-244) resolve to Bravo (zIndex=2). Hit-test ownership measured: y=110,130,150,172,190 → Charlie; y=220,240 → Bravo; y=260,280 → Alpha. Expected: y=148-196 → Bravo; y=196-244 → Alpha. Click-and-expand verification: tap Charlie strip center (y=124) → Charlie expands ✓; tap Bravo strip center (y=172) → NO card expands (toggle noop or dispatched to Charlie then layout settled collapsed) ✗; tap Alpha strip center (y=244) → Alpha expands ✓. Overall 2/3 strip taps route correctly. RCA: `zIndex: cards.length - idx` at /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/cards.tsx:278 is INVERTED. idx=0 gets the HIGHEST zIndex=3 which makes the first (top) card's full 96px tap area override the visible strips of all cards below it. Correct ordering is `zIndex: idx + 1` so each later card (which visually overlays the previous card in the 48px overlap zone) also captures events on that overlay region. REGRESSION PASSES: CRUD (add TEST_Delta, edit TEST_Charlie→TEST_Charlie_Renamed, delete via API) all work; expanded card correctly uses zIndex:20 and sits on top; Schedule modal opens, Minimum/Custom toggle works, schedule-count=250 rows render; empty state unchanged; no LogBox red overlay; no new console errors beyond pre-existing shadow* / pointerEvents RN-web deprecation warnings.

rca_of_issue: The stacked carousel renders N TouchableOpacity cards each with height=96 and marginBottom=-48, creating a 48px visual overlap between adjacent cards. The code sets `zIndex: cards.length - idx` on collapsed cards, giving the first (idx=0) card zIndex=N and the last card zIndex=1. CSS hit-testing uses zIndex: higher zIndex captures pointer events in overlapping regions. Because idx=0 has the HIGHEST zIndex, the first card's full 96px bounding box (y=100-196 for the first card) captures all pointer events in that range — including the 48px (y=148-196) that is Bravo's intended visible-tap-strip. The same cascade continues: Bravo (zIndex=N-1) blocks Alpha's top half. Only the last card's unoccluded bottom half (y=244-292 for Alpha) and the first card's top portion (not overlapped by anything) accept correctly-routed taps. Reproduction: seed 3 cards, go to Cards tab, run `document.elementFromPoint(195, 172)` in dev console — returns first card instead of middle card. Mitigation: invert the ordering to `zIndex: idx + 1` so later DOM cards sit on top in overlap zones, matching the user's visual intent (each visible strip belongs to its own card).
